stem: A client has leg pain and numbness that worsen with standing or walking and improve with sitting or leaning forward. Which disorder best fits this pattern?

options.A: Lumbar spinal stenosis with neurogenic claudication, which typically worsens with lumbar extension or walking and improves with sitting or forward flexion.
options.B: Acute arterial occlusion, because limb ischemia predictably resolves when the client flexes the lumbar spine.
options.C: Isolated hip osteoarthritis, because forward spinal flexion specifically relieves intra-articular hip disease.
options.D: Peripheral neuropathy, because positional relief with sitting or forward flexion is the defining pattern of distal neuropathy.

rationale: NCBI StatPearls identifies posture dependence as a key feature of neurogenic claudication from lumbar spinal stenosis: symptoms are exacerbated by standing, walking, or lumbar extension and improve with sitting or forward flexion. That pattern is much more characteristic of lumbar spinal stenosis than acute arterial occlusion, isolated hip osteoarthritis, or peripheral neuropathy. A is therefore the best answer.
educational_objective: Recognize posture-dependent leg pain or paresthesias that worsen with standing/walking and improve with sitting or forward flexion as the classic pattern of neurogenic claudication from lumbar spinal stenosis.
source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI Bookshelf)

source_claim_supported: Neurogenic claudication from lumbar spinal stenosis characteristically worsens with standing, walking, or lumbar extension and improves with sitting or forward flexion.

source_original.stem: A client has leg pain and numbness that worsen with standing or walking and improve with sitting or leaning forward. Which disorder best fits this pattern?

options.A: Lumbar spinal stenosis with neurogenic claudication that improves when the lumbar spine is flexed
options.B: Acute arterial occlusion because symptoms predictably resolve when the client flexes the lumbar spine
options.C: Isolated hip osteoarthritis because forward spinal flexion specifically relieves intra-articular hip disease
options.D: Peripheral neuropathy because positional relief with sitting is the defining pattern of distal neuropathy

source_original.rationale: Neurogenic claudication from lumbar spinal stenosis commonly worsens with standing or lumbar extension and improves with sitting or forward flexion. The positional pattern helps distinguish it from other causes of leg discomfort.
source_original.source_detail: History and Physical: symptoms worsened by extension/standing or walking and relieved by flexion/sitting; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Verified the NCBI source in the 2026 StatPearls edition, retained the highly characteristic posture-dependent pattern, improved distractor precision, and reduced difficulty from hard to easy because the final item is direct clinical pattern recognition.

audit_findings.currentness: NCBI chapter last updated 2023 and carried in 2026 StatPearls; 2026 systematic-review literature continues to describe the same hallmark pattern.
audit_findings.claim_audit: The final stem and A map directly to the History and Physical description of extension/walking worsening and flexion/sitting relief.

distractor_audit.B: Acute arterial occlusion is not defined by lumbar-flexion relief.
distractor_audit.C: Forward spinal flexion is not a specific relieving sign of hip osteoarthritis.
distractor_audit.D: Peripheral neuropathy is not defined by posture-dependent relief with lumbar flexion.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Vascular claudication can worsen with exertion but the specific relief with sitting/forward lumbar flexion makes neurogenic claudication the best match.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives are plausible causes of lower-extremity symptoms; the positional pattern is the discriminating clinical knowledge.
audit_findings.blueprint: Physiological Adaptation is appropriate for recognition of neurologic/musculoskeletal dysfunction.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-solved against vascular claudication, hip disease, neuropathy, and current NCBI descriptions; A remained uniquely correct with no unsupported thresholds or universal claims.
